A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-training spectral-bias study. Their main texts, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original MLP training results on Gaussian and MNIST data, plus CNN image and patch-covariance experiments.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original MLP/CNN training results, including additional image experiments, covariance-alignment measurements and denoiser-approximation errors.

M1.justification: The explicitly modeled denoiser family expands from one-layer and symmetric two-layer models to untied/deeper linear networks, deep residual networks, and full-width/local circular convolutions (Section 5; Appendices F–G). These introduce different factorization, weight-sharing and locality constraints, while the practical EDM training pipeline is retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds fixed-word and random-word FFHQ image variants (Figure 11; Appendix I.5). Gaussian data, MNIST, CIFAR-10, FFHQ and AFHQ were already represented in v1, including its CNN appendix; extending their use to MLPs does not itself introduce new domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds a direct comparison between CNN-UNet denoiser outputs and a linear convolutional denoiser, reporting approximation MSE across patch sizes and noise scales (Figure 14). v1 contains no analogous denoiser-to-denoiser comparison.

E3.justification: The empirical MLP emergence criterion changes from harmonic to geometric means, with an added exclusion for modes starting within a factor of two of their targets. v2 adds 256/512-dimensional Gaussian configurations and alignment/MSE evaluations. For 64-pixel AFHQ/FFHQ, reported training changes from 50,000 to 250,000 steps, learning rate from 0.0002 to 0.0001, and evaluation samples from 1,000 to 2,000 (Appendix F.5 versus I.6). Unchanged patch plots do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds covariance-eigenframe alignment analyses for MLPs and CNNs (Figures 10 and 13), tests linear-convolution approximation across patch sizes, training stages and noise levels (Figure 14), and adds a fixed-image/noise denoising case study (Figure 15). The earlier CNN patch-size analyses remain in Figures 17–20.

E5.justification: v2 newly identifies noise seed 1019 in Figure 14 and documents fixed-noise comparisons in Figure 15. This is limited case-study seed disclosure; neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds Gaussian configurations, RGB-image MLP results, alignment curves and denoiser-approximation errors. Figure 3 newly reports FFHQ32 MLP exponents of -0.48 and -0.35, with R-squared values 0.97 and 0.92; the FFHQ32 CNN results show near-simultaneous mode emergence. These extend the empirical evidence, while v1's whole-image MNIST and CNN patch plots are retained as Figures 16–20.

T1.justification: v2 adds general regression/ridge proofs, analyses of additional prediction objectives, deep-network dynamics, and convolutional stationary-Gaussian-process and weight-sharing results (Appendices C, F and G). Existing KL and flow-matching derivations remain. The new Lemma 4.1 also introduces a propagator-sign inconsistency with the retained sampling solution in Appendix C.5.

C1.justification: v1's abstract broadly claims robustness of power-law spectral bias in deeper and convolutional architectures. v2 makes the distinction central: MLPs retain the law, whereas convolutional U-Nets exhibit qualitatively different, near-simultaneous emergence. It also adds convolutional dynamics and architectural weight-sharing effects to the main theoretical contributions.

C2.justification: v2 reframes v1's patch-based CNN explanation by distinguishing filter-weight learning from the generated image distribution and proposing locality-induced frequency coupling. It explicitly leaves full convolutional U-Net dynamics unresolved. It also removes v1's specific whitening recommendations and speculation that released large models remain undertrained along small eigenmodes.

D1.justification: New Appendix I.1 specifies single A100/H100 GPUs, training-time estimates, memory use and covariance-computation resources. Appendix I.5 adds configurations for 3072-dimensional RGB-image MLPs. The existing architecture code, EDM loss description and references to supplementary code are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning relative to sampling-time spectral theories, Gaussian-mixture learning, convolutional diffusion theory, deep image priors and neural tangent kernels. New substantive comparisons include Shah et al. and Kamb and Ganguli, beyond v1's narrower discussion of Gaussian structure and regression.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, empirical narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 separates background from learning theory, reorganizes architectural extensions, moves the detailed non-centered analysis into Appendix D, and adds an appendix contents structure. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly single-column layout. New tables summarize theory and loss variants; empirical displays add sample grids, heatmaps, alignment curves and approximation-error plots. Several older figures are retained or relocated, including v1 Figure 3 becoming v2 Figure 21, while the main empirical figures are substantially replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful architectural theory, richer empirical checks and clearer limits on CNN spectral bias. However, central new formulas are inconsistent: Lemma 4.1 reverses the integration limits without changing the exponent sign relative to Appendix C.5, and Equation 10 uses the current Fourier weight where the initial weight is needed. These weaken the reliability of the theoretical expansion, leaving the net quality effect uncertain despite the substantial gains in scope and explanation.
